title: Constructible sheaves are finitely presented; full faithfulness
statement:
Use the universe and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], with $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Put $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$, the category of internal module objects in abelian sheaves on the small pro-etale site, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)\subset\mathcal M$ be the full subcategory of constructible sheaves of [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Here $\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)$ denotes the ordinary ind-category: its objects are small filtered diagrams $C:I\to\mathcal C$, written $\text{“}\varinjlim_i\text{”}C_i$, and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)}(\text{“}\varinjlim_i\text{”}C_i,\text{“}\varinjlim_j\text{”}D_j)=\varprojlim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\varinjlim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(C_i,D_j),$$
with identity and composition induced by identities and composition in $\mathcal C$. Filtered diagrams and their colimits have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The use of a small skeleton of $\mathcal C$ gives the same category up to equivalence.

1. Every $C\in\mathcal C$ is finitely presented as an object of $\mathcal M$: for every small filtered diagram $(M_j)$ in $\mathcal M$, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_j\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(C,M_j)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(C,\varinjlim_jM_j)$$
is bijective.
2. Sending a formal diagram $\text{“}\varinjlim_i\text{”}C_i$ to its actual colimit $\varinjlim_i C_i$ in $\mathcal M$, and sending a represented morphism $C_i\to D_j$ to its composite with $D_j\to\varinjlim_jD_j$, defines a fully faithful functor $\Phi:\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal M$. Its essential image is the full replete subcategory of objects isomorphic to small filtered colimits of constructible sheaves; this subcategory is denoted $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: For either field coefficient ring, apply the constructible-sheaf clause of Ext continuity at degree zero to every small filtered module diagram and its colimit cocone. Compose the degree-zero derived embedding with shift by zero and use the zero-shift isomorphism. This functor is fully faithful by the generic derived single-fully-faithful theorem. Hence ordinary coyoneda is naturally isomorphic to its additive derived Hom functor followed by the forgetful functor from abelian groups. Ext continuity makes the additive comparison invertible, so that functor preserves filtered colimits. The forgetful functor also preserves filtered colimits. Transport preservation along the displayed natural isomorphism to obtain IsFinitelyPresentable for every constructible module. Both coefficient rings have their canonical commutative monoid structures; no equality of underlying sheaves is substituted for their structures.

proof.text: Use coefficient-heart essential smallness for the chosen coefficient ring, giving the small-skeleton prerequisite of the unit. Apply the generic realization theorem to P = IsConstantModelConstructible with the finite-presentability proof of the first step. The ambient coefficient module category already has filtered colimits. Its conclusion supplies the functor, the Yoneda restriction isomorphism, the presentation-colimit clause, fullness, faithfulness, and the precise essential image. Pair this with the finite-presentability statement. Do this for every finite intermediate extension E and for the algebraic closure coefficient; for the latter any finite intermediate extension supplies the otherwise unused E parameter in the Ext-continuity interface.
